title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Clients Under a Disability - Capacity
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal's client suffers a severe traumatic brain injury during an ongoing case, rendering them completely incapable of understanding legal proceedings or giving instructions. There is no continuing power of attorney. What is the paralegal's obligation?
options: Withdraw from the file immediately because the paralegal-client relationship has been frustrated.
Take instructions from the client's closest relative.
Make unilateral decisions for the client based on what the paralegal feels is best.
Take steps to have a lawfully authorized representative, such as a litigation guardian or the Public Guardian and Trustee, appointed to give instructions.
questions.explain: Rule 3.02 outlines that if a client lacks capacity to give instructions and does not have an authorized representative, the paralegal must take steps to ensure one is appointed (such as a litigation guardian) to protect the client's interests. The paralegal cannot take instructions from an unauthorized relative or act unilaterally on major decisions.
